public_id.description:
What the run is named by wherever the destination is not private: the run id itself
where the linked `onevcs`'s public-output check passes it as metadata bound for a
public destination, over every private identity registered on the host, and
otherwise `run-` followed by the first 12 lowercase hex digits of the SHA-256 of the
run id's UTF-8 bytes. Decided once, at the launch, and kept in its record; a run
whose record holds none reads the same derivation over its id.

word.description: The word `status` and `runs` print for the run.

liveness.description: How the run is being driven: the driver-liveness word.

driven.description: Whether anything is driving the run.

ending.description: How the run ended, or `null` for a run that has not.

paused.description: The decision the run is paused on, or `null` for a run that is not.

unanswered.description:
Every command envelope claimed off the run's queue and not answered yet,
in claim order — omitted when there is none.

claim.description:
Where the live driver's claim on its project stands, as its newest read of
it left it — omitted where nothing is known: no driver is live, or the
driver wrote no `claim.json`.

title: RunReading
description:
Whether a run is driven or ended, as one document a script reads:
`onepipeline status <RUN> --json`.

`ending` and `paused` are never both set, and both are `null` while the run is
driven. `schemas/run-reading.schema.json` states the document.

kind.description: Which ending: the run-end hook judge's verdict.

nodes.description:
Every node not `done`, in plan order — the list a failure hook is handed,
and empty for `complete`.

Ending.description: How a run ended, and every node not `done` when it did.

oneOf.description: Every node is `done`: the success hook's ending.
A node is `failed` or `skipped`: the failure hook's `nodes` reason.

A node is not `done`, none failed or skipped, and nothing is left to
decide: the failure hook's `unfinished` reason.

A `stop` was recorded and no driver has adopted the run since: the
failure hook's `stopped` reason.

EndingKind.description: How a run ended: the run-end hook judge's own verdict, read back.

outcome.description: The outcome its settlement recorded, or `null` for a node that recorded none.

EndedNode.description: One node that was not `done` when a run ended — as a failure hook is handed it.

human_actions.description:
Each waiting human action, by node id: completed with `attest`, or
retired with a `drop`.

blocking_surface.description: Whether a blocking planner question is outstanding, answered with `reply`.

Paused.description: The decision a run nothing is driving is paused on.

envelope.description: The channel envelope id — a decimal string in the document.

delivery.description:
Where its live note stands, as the run's live driver last wrote it —
omitted where no driver is live, which leaves the envelope to be answered
by the run's next driver, and where the live driver holds no live note of
it or behind one.

UnansweredEnvelope.description:
One command envelope claimed off a run's queue with no outcome yet, as
`status <RUN> --json` reads it.

node.description: The node whose conversation the note was offered to.

since.description: When it was offered, in epoch milliseconds — RFC 3339 on the wire.

deadline.description:
When the note being offered stops waiting for a turn to take it, in
epoch milliseconds — RFC 3339 on the wire. Present exactly where that
note carries a `delivery_timeout_seconds`, and omitted otherwise.

oneOf.description:
The driver is waiting on `node`'s conversation to answer the envelope's
live note.

node.description: The node whose outstanding note it waits behind.

since.description: When it was first held, in epoch milliseconds — RFC 3339 on the wire.

behind_envelope.description:
The channel envelope id of the envelope whose note it waits behind —
a decimal string on the wire.

oneOf.description:
The driver holds the envelope unjudged behind `behind_envelope`'s live
note to `node`, so that no later edit to that node overtakes it.

Delivery.description:
Where one claimed, unanswered envelope's live note stands, as the run's live
driver last wrote it.

Envelope ids and instants are carried as numbers and written as the strings
the document states — a channel envelope id in decimal, an instant in RFC
3339 — so a value read back that is neither is refused where it is read
rather than shown.

last_confirmed_at.description: When the newest read that confirmed the claim began — `null` where none has.

unconfirmed_since.description: When the claim became unconfirmed — `null` unless it is.

reason.description: Why it is unconfirmed — `null` unless it is.

detail.description:
The newest read's own words: why it confirmed nothing, or the claim that
superseded this driver — `null` where the claim is confirmed.

ClaimReading.description:
The driver's claim, as `status --json` reads it and as `claim.json` carries it.

Instants are carried as epoch milliseconds and written as RFC 3339, as the document
states, so one read back that is not an instant is refused where it is read.

oneOf.description: A read within the lease window found the project this driver's.

No read has confirmed the claim within the lease window: the driver's dispatches in
flight keep running, and it starts no new dispatch and opens no new publication
until a read confirms the claim again.
A read found another driver's claim: this driver ends its dispatches and lets go.

ClaimState.description: Where the driver's claim on its project stands, as its newest read left it.

oneOf.description: The read due did not answer within its deadline.
The read was refused, or answered with something that confirms nothing.

The read was declined for the store's rate limit: refused for it, or not asked
inside a wait the store asked for.

UnconfirmedReason.description: Why no read has confirmed the claim.
